name: Essent Preorder Back in Stock
summary: Shopify pre-order and back-in-stock app: presale and made-to-order campaigns with deposits and split payments, a Notify me waitlist with automatic restock emails, mixed-cart rules and market targeting, with plans tiered by monthly pre-orders and notifications.
best_for: Shopify stores running pre-orders, presales or made-to-order drops that also want a Notify me waitlist with restock emails in the same app, at a few hundred pre-orders a month or fewer, starting on a free plan that already takes deposits
skip_if: you hold stock in several locations and need pre-orders driven by one location's inventory, which a reviewer says the app does not do; you expect one launch to sell far past your plan's allowance and would rather pay a fixed price; or you only need a back-in-stock button and no pre-orders
honest_knock:
The plans are cheap until a launch works. Each paid plan has a monthly allowance and then charges per use: on Lite, the 101st pre-order in a month costs $0.25, and so does every one after it, so a drop that sells 300 pre-orders on Lite costs $4.95 plus $50 in overage. Starter at $8.95 would have covered those 300 without any. Restock alerts are metered the same way, at $1.00 per 100 past the allowance. Pick the plan on the size of the launch you are planning, not on an average month, and check the usage screen while a campaign runs. The free plan's 25 pre-orders is enough to test the flow end to end, and the listing does not say what happens when a free store passes it.

Two features stores often assume are basic sit higher up. Mixed-cart validation, which stops a shopper from putting an in-stock item and a pre-order item in one order, starts on Starter at $8.95, as do campaigns limited to specific markets. A pre-order confirmation email sent from your own domain and scheduled campaigns start on Lite.

The critical reviews are few but specific. A South African store six months in wrote in September 2025 that the app counts inventory across every location, so a store with stock in a physical shop cannot run pre-orders for its online warehouse alone; the developer replied in October 2025 that the request had gone to its development team. An Australian store wrote in June 2026 that after turning the app off with stock back in, its code stayed behind and blocked the checkout button for days; the developer replied after an internal investigation. A US store in August 2025 reported unreliable email delivery and that the pre-order status did not appear on the customer's order confirmation. Earlier one-star reviews describe the app putting every product on pre-order instead of the chosen one, a discount lost when a shopper changed size or quantity, and an admin that would not load; the developer answered each by offering support.

The long list of positive reviews deserves one note. Several reviews were written within the first hour of use, and one UK merchant asked the developer to prompt for a review after three days rather than one hour. The app asks for broad access too: the data-access section lists viewing sensitive customer data and editing customers, products, orders, Shopify Functions and the online store. We installed it on a Shopify development store on 17 November 2026 and created a preorder campaign on an out of stock product, which showed the Preorder button in the theme preview, but the points above come from the listing and the reviews.

pricing.entry_price_terms: Lite · per month for 100 pre-orders and 1,000 back-in-stock notifications, then $0.25 per extra pre-order and $1.00 per 100 extra notifications
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-22 with a plain fetch of apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, which now carries the listing; the essential-preorder address gave a 404 that day: Free and the three paid plans, their allowances, the per-use overage and the $59 Professional plan unchanged, 1,408 reviews at 5.0) (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/essential-preorder and in our own test that day; earlier: read 2026-10-04 on apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, pricing table and data-access section; the vendor's own pricing page at essential-apps.com/pricing lists the apps but no prices) Four plans on the listing plus an unlimited plan mentioned on the top card, priced on two meters: pre-orders a month and back-in-stock notifications a month. Free covers 25 pre-orders and 300 back-in-stock notifications a month, with unlimited Notify me sign-ups, automated pre-orders and restock alerts, variant-level campaigns, full and partial payments, customisable buttons, forms and emails, and 24/7 support. Lite is $4.95 a month for 100 pre-orders and 1,000 notifications, and adds translations, a pre-order confirmation email sent from your own domain, scheduled pre-order campaigns, the Omnisend and Shopify Flow integrations and premium support. Starter is $8.95 a month for 300 pre-orders and 2,500 notifications, and adds campaigns limited to specific markets and mixed-cart validation, with all features included. Essentials is $24.95 a month for 500 pre-orders and 10,000 notifications, with priority support. Past the allowance each paid plan charges per use: $0.25 per extra pre-order on Lite, $0.20 on Starter and $0.10 on Essentials, and $1.00 per 100 extra notifications on all three. The Essentials card adds that unlimited volume is available on a Professional plan at $59 a month. Paid plans carry a 14-day free trial. The listing does not say what happens on the free plan past 25 pre-orders. All charges are in USD; recurring and usage charges are billed through Shopify every 30 days. Developer Essential Apps, with an address in Vilnius, Lithuania; the listing gives a launch date of 22 November 2024 and shows 1,291 reviews, eleven of them at three stars or lower. Read again on 17 November 2026: the listing (the Shopify admin lists the app as Essential Preorder) still shows the Free plan and the three paid plans at the amounts and allowances above, with the $59 Professional plan named on the Essentials card, and now carries 1,399 reviews at 5.0. In our own test the same day on a Shopify development store the app started without a plan choice and without asking for payment, but its plan screen showed no Free card, so we could not find the listing's free allowances of 25 preorders and 300 notifications anywhere in the app. The plan screen showed Lite, Starter, Essentials and Professional with a 30% discount on the first month: Lite $3.47 for the first month and then $4.95, Starter $6.27 then $8.95, Essentials $17.47 then $24.95 and Professional $41.30 then $59, each with a 14 day free trial and a 30 day money back guarantee, and the same allowances as the listing, with Professional unlimited and mixed cart validation from Starter. The first month discount is a temporary offer on the app's screen and is not on the listing, so we do not count it as the price. Shopify's approval screen for Lite read $4.95 every 30 days with $3.47 due for the first period, a 14 day trial ending 1 December and an app spending limit of $500 per 30 days; it listed an Add payment method row and did not carry the line saying the charge would not be billed, so we did not approve it.

compare_with.name: Timesact Preorder
compare_with.why: Timesact Preorder is the closest app in our own dossiers. On our reading of 25 September 2026 Timesact's free plan covered 20 orders a month, its usage-based CORE Flexible plan started at $5 a month for 10 orders and $17 for 100, with $0.20 per order past the volume you pick, and its CORE Fixed plan covered unlimited orders for $23 a month on a Basic Shopify store, rising to $117 on Shopify Plus. Essent Preorder Back in Stock, read on 4 October 2026, gives 25 pre-orders and 300 restock alerts free, 100 pre-orders for $4.95 and 300 for $8.95, with unlimited volume on a $59 Professional plan. At low and medium volume Essent is the cheaper of the two; a Basic Shopify store that regularly passes a few hundred pre-orders a month pays less on Timesact's fixed plan. Both bundle back-in-stock alerts with pre-orders and take deposits.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Preorder (reviewed as Essent Preorder Back in Stock) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the app opening without a plan choice or a card, a preorder campaign for The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available) published in the app, then the badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and the button Preorder in an unsaved theme preview after the app embed was switched on by hand (about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks from the install; the embed was switched off again), the plans screen with four paid plans and a 30% first month discount, the Shopify approval screen for Lite (a 14-day trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved), after which the campaign was deleted and the app uninstalled. The back in stock alert, mixed carts and deposits were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the app was installed from its App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, called Essential Preorder in the admin) through the install form with the target set to the same tab, in our own tab, from 21:45:24; the first submit only showed the Apps page, the second showed the dialog Install app, and Install was clicked. The app opened without a plan choice and without a payment step, with a Setup Guide at 0 / 3 completed. No separate account, password, card or phone number was asked. Core action, a preorder campaign for a product with no stock: Create preorder campaign, the tab Preorder products, Add specific products, The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available), Publish. The message was Campaign created successfully., the status was Live, and a banner said Essent Preorder Back in Stock app is not activated yet. The app preview showed a sample product (White T-shirt) with a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder. In the theme editor (unsaved preview of the product) the product showed, without the app embed, a choice One-time Purchase $885.95 and Preorder $885.95 (a selling plan) with Add to cart. With the embed Essential Preorder switched on, the preview showed a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder, with an overlay Click "Save" to enable the app embed. The embed was switched off again, nothing was saved (Leave page) and the store itself was not looked at (it has a password). The first result, the Preorder button in the preview, came at about 21:48:15, about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks after the install, including the plans page and choosing the product. Plans in the app (the plans screen, each with Start FREE 14 days trial and 30 day money back guarantee, and a label -30% first mo): Lite $3.47 first month, then $4.95 a month, 100 preorders and 1000 back in stock notifications a month; Starter $6.27 first month, then $8.95, 300 preorders and 2500 notifications, with mixed cart validation; Essentials $17.47 first month, then $24.95, 500 preorders and 10000 notifications; Professional $41.3 first month, then $59, unlimited. Using the app was free by default: it opened without a card. The free limits of the listing (25 preorders, 300 notifications) were not seen in the app, because the plans screen has no Free card. Checkout: Start FREE 14 days trial on Lite opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan LITE, $4,95 $3,47 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $3,47 due 1 Dec, an App spending limit of a maximum of $500,00 USD per 30 days, a row Add payment method and a greyed Approve button. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed, so the plan was not approved. No card was entered. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was no cancel button to look for. The uninstall dialog (Uninstall Essential Preorder?) says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and asks for a Reason for uninstalling, which is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled (You've successfully uninstalled Essential Preorder). Differences from the review: the listing names the Lite price as $4.95; the app shows the same regular prices and a 30% discount on the first month. The free limits of the listing were not seen. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: the back in stock alert and restock e-mails, mixed carts, deposits and split payment, the real checkout, the store itself (it has a password), the paid plans and their approval, and any contact with the vendor. Clean up: the campaign was deleted (the confirmation was Yes, turn off Continue selling); our notes say that the stock was never changed and that no test product was made, the existing product was used. The embed was not saved. The app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The preorder button only showed once the app embed was switched on by hand in the theme editor; the app says so in a banner. The free limits of the listing (25 preorders and 300 notifications) were not visible in the app, because the plans screen shows only paid plans. The Lite approval screen needed a payment method, so a test charge could not be approved.

sessions.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Essential Preorder (reviewed as Essent Preorder Back in Stock) on a Shopify development store: the install through the install form, the app opening without a plan choice or a card, a preorder campaign for The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available) published in the app, then the badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and the button Preorder in an unsaved theme preview after the app embed was switched on by hand (about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks from the install; the embed was switched off again), the plans screen with four paid plans and a 30% first month discount, the Shopify approval screen for Lite (a 14-day trial; it asked for a payment method and had no test charge sentence; nothing approved), after which the campaign was deleted and the app uninstalled. The back in stock alert, mixed carts and deposits were not tested. Nothing was paid. Install: the app was installed from its App Store listing (apps.shopify.com/essential-pre-order, called Essential Preorder in the admin) through the install form with the target set to the same tab, in our own tab, from 21:45:24; the first submit only showed the Apps page, the second showed the dialog Install app, and Install was clicked. The app opened without a plan choice and without a payment step, with a Setup Guide at 0 / 3 completed. No separate account, password, card or phone number was asked. Core action, a preorder campaign for a product with no stock: Create preorder campaign, the tab Preorder products, Add specific products, The Out of Stock Snowboard (0 available), Publish. The message was Campaign created successfully., the status was Live, and a banner said Essent Preorder Back in Stock app is not activated yet. The app preview showed a sample product (White T-shirt) with a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder. In the theme editor (unsaved preview of the product) the product showed, without the app embed, a choice One-time Purchase $885.95 and Preorder $885.95 (a selling plan) with Add to cart. With the embed Essential Preorder switched on, the preview showed a badge Preorder, the line Ships as soon as possible and a button Preorder, with an overlay Click "Save" to enable the app embed. The embed was switched off again, nothing was saved (Leave page) and the store itself was not looked at (it has a password). The first result, the Preorder button in the preview, came at about 21:48:15, about 3 minutes and about 12 clicks after the install, including the plans page and choosing the product. Plans in the app (the plans screen, each with Start FREE 14 days trial and 30 day money back guarantee, and a label -30% first mo): Lite $3.47 first month, then $4.95 a month, 100 preorders and 1000 back in stock notifications a month; Starter $6.27 first month, then $8.95, 300 preorders and 2500 notifications, with mixed cart validation; Essentials $17.47 first month, then $24.95, 500 preorders and 10000 notifications; Professional $41.3 first month, then $59, unlimited. Using the app was free by default: it opened without a card. The free limits of the listing (25 preorders, 300 notifications) were not seen in the app, because the plans screen has no Free card. Checkout: Start FREE 14 days trial on Lite opened the Shopify screen Approve subscription with the plan LITE, $4,95 $3,47 USD every 30 days, You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., Total $3,47 due 1 Dec, an App spending limit of a maximum of $500,00 USD per 30 days, a row Add payment method and a greyed Approve button. The screen did NOT say that a test charge would not be billed, and a payment method was needed, so the plan was not approved. No card was entered. Cancelling: no paid plan was started, so there was no cancel button to look for. The uninstall dialog (Uninstall Essential Preorder?) says that you can no longer use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and asks for a Reason for uninstalling, which is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled (You've successfully uninstalled Essential Preorder). Differences from the review: the listing names the Lite price as $4.95; the app shows the same regular prices and a 30% discount on the first month. The free limits of the listing were not seen. The price fields are not changed here. Not tested: the back in stock alert and restock e-mails, mixed carts, deposits and split payment, the real checkout, the store itself (it has a password), the paid plans and their approval, and any contact with the vendor. Clean up: the campaign was deleted (the confirmation was Yes, turn off Continue selling); our notes say that the stock was never changed and that no test product was made, the existing product was used. The embed was not saved. The app was uninstalled in Settings, Apps. Our own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
